rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so I am raising obfuscation pressure across all seven passes for this tiny 12-function trie benchmark. SUB stays the workhorse (near-zero cost, strong arithmetic diversification) with the highest security weight; BCF is pushed close behind since the 1.4KB text budget can absorb modest bogus-block inflation while static analysis of trie_insert/trie_scan gets much harder. FLA and IGV keep moderate CorrectnessRisk weights because flattening loop-carried trie traversal and encrypting globals (trie node tables, charsequence buffers) are the two passes most likely to introduce subtle breakage in pointer-heavy code, so the compiler applies them selectively where features favor them. SPLIT gets high cost-dimension tolerance and low risk because it is nearly free and synergizes with FLA/BCF by creating more basic blocks to scramble; IBR and ICALL diversify the call/branch graph (charsequence_push and addfile call sites) at acceptable runtime cost. Overall the table favors diversity and security now that correctness is demonstrated, while keeping RuntimeCost weights below 0.65 for FLA/ICALL so the hot trie lookup loop is not excessively flattened or indirected.
